analysis:
This batch contains only test changes. It adds no new attack surface.

The tests describe new production behavior that is not in this batch:
- A new displayedProviderAuthorization / ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.displayedStatus path.
- A two-argument summary(displayed, removalAuthorization:).

What the head tests assert (ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests.swift):
- Display may keep showing an unexpired App Attest lease after the renewal is older than snapshotMaxAge (lines 102-132).
- Display still requires all of the following: path app_attest, status online, matching process identity, matching coordinator URL, a finite unexpired expiry, receivedAt after startedAt, and writtenAt fresh (lines 124-131, 183-189).
- MDM removal readiness (currentProviderAuthorization) keeps the stricter receipt window (lines 121-122, 181-182, 192-208).
- summary offers unenroll only when the removal decision matches the displayed grant's session, machine, reason, mdmRemovalReady and protocol (lines 224-249).
- A removal decision cannot restore a missing or expired displayed grant (lines 251-260).
- CLI test StatusCommandRunTests.swift lines 282-305 asserts that status shows App Attest authorization but no unenroll offer for a late renewal.

Threat-model relevance:
- This is a local, operator-facing diagnostic only.
- Per TB-002 and TB-011, local status and doctor verdicts are not trust evidence. Serving authorization is enforced by the coordinator: authorizeInferenceHandoff and expiry/revocation per T-053.
- So the wider display window cannot grant serving.
- The removal path, which matters for T-057 (premature MDM removal stranding a provider), stays bound to the fresh receipt window per the tests.

Why no finding was raised:
- Nothing in this batch is a regression.
- The implementation is outside this batch, so test intent is not proof of behavior.

Questions for integration:
- Verify the production sources: DaemonState.displayedProviderAuthorization, ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.displayedStatus and summary.
- Confirm that doctor and unenroll pass currentProviderAuthorization, not the displayed status, as removalAuthorization.
- Confirm that unenroll itself gates on removalReady(current), not on summary text.
- Confirm that the session/machine/reason equality check is implemented.
